diagnostic_evidence.quote: The associated sesquilinear inner product~$(u,v)_\calD := \int_\calD u(\bx) \overline{v}(\bx) \dd \bx$

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's inner product convention, (\partial_t\psi, e^{-t/T}\partial_t\psi) is a nonnegative real number (the displayed identity), so Re(i(\partial_t\psi, w)) = 0, not \int_0^T |\partial_s\psi|^2 e^{-s/T} ds as the proof claims. The correct conclusion is 0 = \mu[(1/2T)\int_0^T|\psi|^2 e^{-s/T}ds + (1/2e)|\psi(T)|^2], which gives \psi\equiv 0 for \mu\neq 0 (and \mu=0 is immediate). Thus the displayed equation is false and, as written, the argument yields uniqueness only for \mu>0, but the proposition's statement (all real \mu) survives the correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the final displayed equation by 0 = (\mu/2T)\int_0^T|\psi|^2 e^{-s/T}ds + (\mu/2e)|\psi(T)|^2, conclude \psi\equiv 0 for \mu\neq 0, and note that for \mu=0 the equation i(\partial_t\psi,\partial_t\psi)=0 forces \partial_t\psi=0.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness proof of prop:32 contains a false intermediate identity; the proposition's conclusion for all real \mu remains true after a one-line correction. No other formal result depends on prop:32.
issues.title: False term in the real-part identity of the continuous uniqueness proof (prop:32)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single forced correction (Re(i\cdot(\text{real}))=0) in one proof step; the statement and all its consequences are preserved, with no new lemma or loss of scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If~$|\mu| < \pi/T$, then problem \eqref{eq:10} has a unique solution.

issues.failure_explanation: The real part of the displayed equation is \mu(|\psi_h^p(T)|^2 - Re(\partial_t\psi_h^p,\psi_h^p)) = 0, so the inference |\psi_h^p(T)|^2 = Re(\partial_t\psi_h^p,\psi_h^p) divides by \mu and is vacuous at \mu=0, which is included in the hypothesis |\mu|<\pi/T. For \mu=0 the conclusion still follows immediately from the same equation (i\|\partial_t\psi_h^p\|^2=0), so the statement is correct but the case split has an unstated sub-case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the \mu=0 sub-case explicitly: then eq:17 gives i\|\partial_t\psi_h^p\|_{L^2}^2=0, hence \psi_h^p\equiv 0; for \mu\neq 0 the displayed real-part argument applies as written.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of prop:33 does not cover \mu=0 in its real-part step; the proposition's conclusion is unaffected because the imaginary part gives \|\partial_t\psi_h^p\|^2=0 directly when \mu=0.
issues.title: Uncovered \mu=0 case in the discrete uniqueness proof (prop:33)
issues.why_classification: A missing sub-case with an immediate trivial argument; adding one line repairs the proof completely and the statement, rate, and scope are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For p=1 hat functions, (\partial_t\phi_\ell^1, \partial_t\phi_{\ell-1}^1) = -1/h and (\partial_t\phi_\ell^1, \phi_{\ell-1}^1) = 1/2 (equivalently, the symbol polynomials q^{\mathbf{B}^1}(z)=-(1-z)^2 and q^{\mathbf{C}^1}(z)=(z^2-1)/2), so the diagonal of \mathbf{K}_h^1(\mu)=i\mathbf{B}_h^1-\mu\mathbf{C}_h^1 is -(i/h+\mu/2), not -(8i/h+\mu/2). The coefficient 8 is a miscalculation; the remark's conclusion (invertibility for all h>0, \mu\in\mathbb{R}, hence plausibility of assu:34 for p=1) is unaffected.

failure_location.quote: Indeed, in this case, the system matrix stemming from~\eqref{eq:10} is a lower triangular matrix with entries all equal to~$ -\left(8\mi/h +\mu/2\right)$ on the diagonal.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the diagonal entries to -(i/h+\mu/2), computed from \mathbf{B}^1[\ell,\ell]=-1/h and \mathbf{C}^1[\ell,\ell]=1/2.
issues.overall_effect: The stated diagonal of the p=1 system matrix is incorrect, but the remark's purpose — invertibility of the p=1 system matrix for all h and \mu — remains valid, so nothing substantive is lost.
issues.title: Wrong diagonal entries of the p=1 system matrix in the remark after assu:34
issues.why_classification: A wrong constant in an illustrative claim with a forced correction and no effect on any guarantee or downstream argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Two errors compound here. (i) By linearity of the symbol map applied to \mathbf{K}_n^p(\rho)=i\mathbf{B}_n^p-\rho\mathbf{C}_n^p, one gets q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho)}=i q^{\mathbf{B}^p}-\rho q^{\mathbf{C}^p}, not eq:25. (ii) The displayed expansion of q^{\mathbf{C}^p} satisfies a_{2p-j}=-a_j (skew-reciprocal), not a_{2p-j}=a_j, and the sum of a reciprocal and a skew-reciprocal polynomial is not reciprocal for \rho\neq 0 (e.g., p=1: q^{\mathbf{K}^1(\rho)}(z)=(\rho-i)+2iz+(-i-\rho)z^2 has roots 1 and (1+i\rho)/(1-i\rho), but the reciprocal of the second root is not a root). The correct structure is anti-self-inversive: since q^{\mathbf{B}^p} is reciprocal and q^{\mathbf{C}^p} skew-reciprocal with real coefficients, the coefficients of q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho)} satisfy a_{2p-j}=-\overline{a_j}, so off-circle zeros pair as \xi,1/\overline{\xi} and the type (p-1,2,p-1) conclusion still follows. The proposition's conclusion is therefore repairable in place, but the proof as written asserts a false central claim.

failure_location.quote: In particular, from these expressions, both $q^{\B^p}$ and $q^{\C^p}$ are reciprocal polynomials, and from \eqref{eq:25}, it follows that $q^{\K^p(\rho)}$ is also a reciprocal polynomial for all $\rho \in \R$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the reciprocity claim by the correct anti-self-inversive structure: from q^{\mathbf{B}^p} reciprocal and q^{\mathbf{C}^p} skew-reciprocal with real coefficients, q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho)}=iq^{\mathbf{B}^p}-\rho q^{\mathbf{C}^p} satisfies a_{2p-j}=-\overline{a_j}; then zeros pair as \xi,1/\overline{\xi}, giving type (\ell,2p-2\ell,\ell), and correct eq:25 accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The justification of the symbol type in prop:39 is invalid (false reciprocity claim and wrong linear relation eq:25). The proposition's conclusion (weak well-conditioning given two unit-modulus zeros) survives via the correct self-inversive symmetry, so th:313 and th:42 remain valid after repair, but the argument as written does not prove what it claims.
issues.title: False reciprocity claim for the symbol polynomial q^{K^p(\rho)} (prop:39)
issues.why_classification: The proof's central structural claim is false and must be replaced by a different symmetry argument (anti-self-inversivity); this is a contained but nontrivial correction rather than a typo fix, although the proposition's conclusion and all downstream results survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For~$\rho>0$ and~$p \in \mathbb{N}$, the function $K_p(\theta,\rho)$ has exactly 2 simple zeros 
$\theta \in [-\pi,\pi]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of prop:312 actually covers every \rho\neq 0 (the monotonicity argument never uses \rho>0, and \theta=0 is simple since \partial_\theta K_p(0)=-\rho\neq 0), but at \rho=0 one has K_p(\theta,0)=-B_p(\theta), which has a single double zero at \theta=0 (since B_p(\theta)\sim -\theta^2), so the 'exactly two simple zeros' conclusion fails there. The case \rho=0 (i.e., \mu=0) is part of the advertised range 'for all \rho\in\mathbb{R}' of th:313 but is not covered by the argument; it is recoverable because q^{\mathbf{K}^p(0)}=iq^{\mathbf{B}^p} has a double zero at z=1 and, q^{\mathbf{B}^p} being reciprocal, type (p-1,2,p-1), or via the cited weak conditioning of \{\mathbf{B}_h^p\}.

failure_location.quote: Let Assumption \ref{assu:34} be satisfied. Then, for all~$p \in \N$ and~$\rho \in \R$, the family of matrices~$\{\K_n^p(\rho)\}_n$ defined in~\eqref{eq:21} is weakly well-conditioned.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the \rho=0 case: K_p(\theta,0)=-B_p(\theta) vanishes only at \theta=0 with multiplicity two, so q^{\mathbf{K}^p(0)}=iq^{\mathbf{B}^p} is of type (p-1,2,p-1) and Theorem th:38(b) applies; alternatively cite Prop.~3.10 of FFLP2024 for the weak well-conditioning of \{\mathbf{B}_h^p\}.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of th:313 establishes weak well-conditioning only for \rho\neq 0; the claim for all \rho\in\mathbb{R} is unsupported at \rho=0, where the symbol has a double zero at z=1 instead of two simple zeros. th:42 uses th:313 only at \rho=\sqrt{\mu_w}h>0 and is unaffected.
issues.title: Zero-counting argument of th:313 does not cover \rho=0
issues.why_classification: Only the single parameter value \rho=0 is missing, and it is recoverable by a two-line symbol argument or a cited result; the advertised statement, method, and guarantees all survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let Assumption \ref{assu:34} be satisfied. Then, for all~$p \in \N$ and~$\rho \in \R$, the family of matrices~$\{\K_n^p(\rho)\}_n$ defined in~\eqref{eq:21} is weakly well-conditioned.
Assume that, for all $p \in \N$ with $p \ge 1$, $h>0$, and $\mu_w > 0$ the variational formulation~\eqref{eq:30} admits a unique solution.

issues.failure_explanation: th:313 requires assu:34 (uniqueness of the Schrödinger formulation eq:10 for all p, h, \mu), but th:42 assumes uniqueness only for the wave formulation eq:30, and the implication from the latter to the former is not argued. The implication does hold for \mu>0 — uniqueness of eq:30 is equivalent (via invertibility of \mathbf{B}_h^p and the Schur complement \mathbf{B}+\mu_w\mathbf{C}\mathbf{B}^{-1}\mathbf{C}) to uniqueness of eq:32 with \mu_s^2=\mu_w, hence by prop:41 to assu:34 for \mu>0 — but this chain is missing, and the sentence claiming the Schur complements are weakly well-conditioned 'for all \mu_s\in\mathbb{R}' overreaches the justified range \mu_s>0. The stability transfer from eq:10 to eq:32 (realification) is likewise asserted without argument.

failure_location.quote: Theorem \ref{th:313} guarantees the stability of the variational formulation~\eqref{eq:10}, and, consequently, that of~\eqref{eq:32}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the short justification that th:42's hypothesis plus invertibility of \mathbf{B}_h^p (Prop.~3.10 of FFLP2024) and the Schur-complement form \mathbf{B}+\mu\mathbf{C}\mathbf{B}^{-1}\mathbf{C} imply assu:34 for \mu>0 via prop:41, and restrict the claim to \mu_s>0.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof of th:42 invokes th:313 outside its hypothesis; the unconditional-stability conclusion for eq:30 is still correct but rests on an unestablished dependency, and the stated range 'for all \mu_s\in\mathbb{R}' is unjustified.
issues.title: th:42 applies th:313 without establishing Assumption assu:34
issues.why_classification: The missing justification is a short, contained chain of standard equivalences; the theorem's conclusion and scope (\mu_w>0) are fully preserved once it is added.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Likewise, let~$\bM_{h_{\bx}}$ and~$\A_{h_{\bx}}$ denote the spatial mass matrix and the matrix representing the discretization of the Hamiltonian operator, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: With \mathbf{A}_{h_x} the discretization of the Hamiltonian \tfrac12\Delta+V (i.e., -\tfrac12 stiffness + V-mass, matching eq:7), testing with \partial_t\widehat{W}, \widehat{W}\in S_{h,\bullet,0}^p\otimes S_{h_x} and using (\phi_j,\partial_t\phi_{\ell-1})_{J_T}=-\mathbf{C}^p_{h_t}[\ell,j] (integration by parts; boundary terms vanish since trial splines vanish at 0 and test splines at T) yields (i\mathbf{B}_{h_t}^p\otimes\mathbf{M}_{h_x}-\mathbf{C}_{h_t}^p\otimes\mathbf{A}_{h_x})\boldsymbol{\Psi}=\mathbf{F}. The plus sign in eq:35 is therefore inconsistent with the variational formulation unless \mathbf{A}_{h_x} is defined as the negated Hamiltonian, contradicting the prose definition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change eq:35 to (i\mathbf{B}_{h_t}^p\otimes\mathbf{M}_{h_x}-\mathbf{C}_{h_t}^p\otimes\mathbf{A}_{h_x})\boldsymbol{\Psi}=\mathbf{F}, or equivalently define \mathbf{A}_{h_x} as the discretization of -(\tfrac12\Delta+V).
issues.overall_effect: The global linear system as written does not correspond to method eq:7 for the stated Hamiltonian discretization; an implementation following eq:35 literally assembles the wrong system. The formal stability results are independent of this sign error.
issues.title: Wrong sign in the global linear system eq:35
issues.why_classification: A single sign change (or a negated definition of \mathbf{A}_{h_x}) restores full consistency with the variational formulation; no mathematical content is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The correct Bartels–Stewart reduction of (i\mathbf{B}\otimes\mathbf{M}+\mathbf{C}\otimes\mathbf{A})\boldsymbol{\Psi}=\mathbf{F} with \mathbf{G}=(i\mathbf{B})^{-1}\mathbf{C}=\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{R}\mathbf{Q}^H is (\mathbf{I}\otimes\mathbf{M}+\mathbf{R}\otimes\mathbf{A})\mathbf{Z}=(i\mathbf{B})^{-1}\mathbf{Q}^H\otimes\mathbf{I})\mathbf{F}, \boldsymbol{\Psi}=(\mathbf{Q}\otimes\mathbf{I})\mathbf{Z}. The algorithm instead uses (\mathbf{R}\otimes\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{R}^{-1}\otimes\mathbf{M}) in step 4 (not similar to the correct matrix under the stated substitutions), drops the factor i in step 2, and has a spurious minus sign in step 5. Already for 1x1 blocks the algorithm returns \psi=icf/(b^2m-c^2a) instead of f/(ibm+ca), so it does not solve eq:35 (nor the corrected minus-sign version).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the Bartels–Stewart steps: with \mathbf{G}=(i\mathbf{B}_{h_t}^p)^{-1}\mathbf{C}_{h_t}^p=\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{R}\mathbf{Q}^H, solve (\mathbf{I}\otimes\mathbf{M}_{h_x}+\mathbf{R}^p_{h_t}\otimes\mathbf{A}_{h_x})\mathbf{Z}=(\mathbf{Q}^H(i\mathbf{B}_{h_t}^p)^{-1}\otimes\mathbf{I})\mathbf{F} and set \boldsymbol{\Psi}=(\mathbf{Q}_{h_t}^p\otimes\mathbf{I})\mathbf{Z} (equivalently, fix step 2 to (i\mathbf{B}_{h_t}^p\otimes\mathbf{I})\mathbf{Y}=\mathbf{F}, step 4 to (\mathbf{I}\otimes\mathbf{M}_{h_x}+\mathbf{R}^p_{h_t}\otimes\mathbf{A}_{h_x})\mathbf{Z}=\mathbf{Y}, and step 5 to \boldsymbol{\Psi}=(\mathbf{Q}_{h_t}^p\otimes\mathbf{I})\mathbf{Z}).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised efficient solver fails its input-output contract: as stated it computes a wrong solution of the space-time system. The theoretical results and the reported numerical experiments do not depend on the algorithm block, so the loss is confined to the solver description.
issues.title: Algorithm alg:1 does not solve the system eq:35
issues.why_classification: Three of the five steps implement the wrong transformation, so the procedure must be re-derived along the standard Bartels–Stewart reduction; this is a contained rewrite using the cited template, but it is more than a local patch, and the algorithm as stated delivers no correct guarantee.
